title: 灵犀 task event
description: What an agent tells the cat about the work it is doing. This is the ONE surface every integration targets: Claude Code hooks, a Codex notify program, an MCP tool call, a shell script or a bare curl all produce this object and nothing else. Adding a fourth host means writing an adapter that emits this - it never means changing the app. The split that matters: `state` and `kind` describe a PROCESS and a host can supply them from lifecycle events alone. `mood` describes the PERSON, and only something that has read the work can judge it - which is why a plugin can guarantee a baseline reaction while only the model can make it feel like the cat knows what is going on.

state.description: Where the work has got to. The only required field. `needs_input` and `needs_approval` are deliberately separate: a question can wait until the user looks up, an approval is blocking a tool call right now, and a notification outlet needs to be able to treat them differently.

kind.description: What sort of work it is. Lets the cat react differently to a failed deploy than to a failed search.

mood.description: How the work FEELS - the dimension that makes this a pet rather than a status light. Someone writing to their mother and someone fighting a flaky test are both running/write. Judge the mood of the WORK, not your own confidence in it: you can be certain about an apology letter and it is still `sad`. The cat ANSWERS the mood rather than mirroring it - failure is met with comfort, not alarm - so reporting a bad mood honestly is safe. Hosts that only see lifecycle events should omit this rather than guess.

progress.description: 0..1 where known. Send it freely: `running` updates are swallowed except the first and the crossing of halfway, so a progress stream does not become a reaction stream. Terminal states are never swallowed.

summary.description: One line, in the user's language, about what just happened. Shown in the cat's speech bubble when the reaction includes one.

provider.description: Which tool this came from - "claude-code", "codex", a CI name. Used for grouping in the event log.

agent.description: The registered agent id this is attributed to (see POST /agents). Determines whose logo appears on the speech bubble when several agents share one cat. Omitted means anonymous, which the user cannot tell apart from any other anonymous caller.

taskId.description: Stable id for this piece of work across its lifetime. Progress suppression is keyed on it, so reusing one id for unrelated work will silently swallow reactions.

session.description: The host's long-lived session this event belongs to (a Claude Code session id). When set, 主界面 keeps one activity row per session instead of one per agent, so several sessions of the same tool can be told apart.

label.description: A human name for that session - the host's own title for it, or the project folder. Shown on the speech bubble beside the agent's mark and on the 主界面 row. Display only: the app never forwards it to a notification sink or keeps it in the event log.

result.description: What this turn came to, in the host's own words (for Claude Code, its last reply). The app takes one bubble-sized line from it so the cat talks about THIS task, and keeps none of it: it is never written to the event log or disk, and never forwarded to a notification sink. Keep `summary` free of work content; put it here.
